 Costco recalls whipped cream over possible cleaning chemical contamination
 According to a notice sent to Costco members, some customers have reported a chemical smell and taste, but no serious illnesses have been reported. 
 Prev 
 Next 
 Alamance Foods, Inc. 
 Cans of recalled whipped cream 
 By: 
 Scripps News Group 
 Posted 
 and last updated 
 Share Copy link Facebook Nextdoor X Threads Reddit LinkedIn Email WhatsApp Messenger Print 
 Add Scripps News as a Google Preferred Source 
 A recall has been issued for cans of Costco's Kirkland Signature whipped cream because they may have been contaminated with a cleaning chemical.
 The recall involves whipped cream cans, manufactured by Alamance Foods, sold between Oct. 11 and Oct. 31. 
 According to a notice sent to Costco members, some customers have reported a chemical smell and taste, but no serious illnesses have been reported. 
 IN CASE YOU MISSED IT | More than 200,000 Sharper Image fire pits recalled due to burn risks 
 The affected products have a "Best If Used By" date of April 2, 2027, and timestamps ranging from 00:35 to 02:45 printed on the cans. The Costco item number is 1777000.
 The recalled whipped cream was sold in the following states:
 Alabama
 Florida
 Georgia
 Illinois
 Indiana
 Iowa
 Mississippi
 Missouri
 North Carolina
 South Carolina
 Tennessee
 Wisconsin
 Customers who purchased the affected whipped cream should stop using it immediately and return it to their local Costco for a full refund.
 The company has not explained how a cleaning chemical may have contaminated the product or how it may have entered the cans.
